title: Content deduplication and native version identity under benign updates
research_question: Can a successful same-value or existing-value native update make its requested value unavailable through the public current-memory interface, without injected faults?
rationale: The pinned update_memory dedup branch rewrites the returned record's predecessor after archiving the old ID. Equality between those IDs and reuse of an existing predecessor are source-informed edge cases not exercised by the inspected upstream dedup tests.
scope: Two pinned native Python memory configurations, literal synthetic content, sequential public calls, one workstation. These are different interfaces, not a shared reliability ranking.
hypothesis: In agentmem's same-value update path, content deduplication can return the old ID, after which archiving and predecessor assignment can hide the requested current value and introduce a self edge despite a successful API outcome.
null_hypothesis: Successful benign updates retain the requested value through the current-memory interface and preserve a noncyclic native predecessor graph where applicable.
primary_metric: Per fixed stream: successful final API outcome and absence of requested value in public current-memory observation, verified by native storage observations and cold reopen.
secondary_metrics: Before/after public history of pre-existing other chains
acceptable_evidence: Raw native responses, public current-memory reads, native history, physical storage snapshots, source bindings, cold reopen and preserved stores.
gold_reference: Literal requested value and native storage records. No semantic human labels. Native predecessor graph is NOT_APPLICABLE to Mem0 event history.
population: The fixed authored streams only. No production error rate or adoption inference.
sample_size_plan: Eight streams times two native configurations times two fresh repetitions equals 32 cells.
split_policy: New source-informed development study. Cases were selected after source inspection, not a held-out or confirmatory sample. Earlier null comparison is preserved.
intervention: Benign value and identity relationships among public add/remember and update calls. No fault, source patch, semantic extraction, model or external service.
matched_control: Ordinary new-value change, repeated remember/add, return to an archived value, and identical value in another namespace.
analysis_plan: Retain all 32 cells. Report outcomes by stream and interface, graph diagnostics only where natively applicable, and agreement across the two fresh repetitions. No aggregate framework accuracy, population inference or significance test.
failure_criteria: Stop interpretation on source mismatch, missing cell, unreadable observation, unexpected network attempt, sentinel change, cold-reopen drift, or invalid normal control. Expected behavioral counterexamples do not stop the fixed matrix.
budget: Existing local Python 3.12 environments and cached dependencies only. Zero model or embedding API calls, zero new human labels.
ethics: Synthetic content, private local outputs, no public bug report, source patch, commit or submission.
closest_prior_work: Pinned agentmem TestUpdateMemoryDedup explicitly checks distinct existing IDs, not same-ID reuse
Established content deduplication and version graph principles
Prior Mem0 partial-write issues do not establish this benign-call result
MemTxn and SLM already use history and state invariants; no new general observation method is claimed
baselines: Unmodified Mem0 2.2.1 with local Qdrant and SQLite event history; static embedding double
Unmodified agentmem-lite 0.3.0 source at pinned commit; sqlite-vec active with no embedding function
Normal and namespace controls within each interface
quality_checks: Public observation reconciled with actual stores
No network during native imports and execution

interpretation_rules.same_value_loss: A successful final update followed by no requested current value, matching the physical state and persisting after cold reopen, supports a bounded benign-call failure witness.
interpretation_rules.other_chain_change: Record the exact changed predecessor/history. This diagnostic does not assume an undocumented immutable multi-parent history contract or count such a change as a primary violation.
interpretation_rules.different_interfaces: Report Mem0 event history and agentmem predecessor graphs separately. Mem0 graph outcomes remain NOT_APPLICABLE.
interpretation_rules.no_superiority: A comprehensive check is expected to detect these effects. No diagnostic superiority or new transaction principle follows.
interpretation_rules.novelty: Exact native-case novelty and publication significance require a separate primary-source audit. Successful reproduction is not sufficient.
